interpolation.description_plain_english: Using a value in between two listed table values when the measured angle falls between them, retaining one decimal place of precision.
interpolation.how_the_guide_uses_it: The assessor uses interpolation when a measurement falls between two values in a table, so the final incapacity percentage is estimated between the two nearest listed percentages instead of jumping abruptly from one to the other. The decimal fraction is retained.

whole-numbers-first rule for fractions.description_plain_english: When combining impairment values that include fractions, combine the whole-number parts first and then add the leftover fraction back at the end.
whole-numbers-first rule for fractions.how_the_guide_uses_it: When the guide converts a range-of-motion loss into a percentage using a fraction, the calculation is done with whole numbers before rounding so the final rating is mathematically consistent.

partial loss halving rule.description_plain_english: When assessing partial sensory or motor loss, the guide awards exactly 50% of the maximum value for total loss, retaining any decimal fraction (e.g., 2.5%) without rounding it up.
partial loss halving rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule prevents inflation of impairment percentages by ensuring that half-values are kept exact, rather than being rounded to the nearest whole number.

nearest-5-percent rule.description_plain_english: Some chapter ratings are expressed to the nearest 5%.
nearest-5-percent rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: After a class-based percentage is worked out in these chapters, the result is rounded to the nearest 5% so the final award fits the guide’s rating scale.

14-hour noise-free rule.description_plain_english: Before formal audiometric examination, there should be at least 14 hours without noise exposure so that temporary threshold shift does not distort the result.
14-hour noise-free rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: Before the formal hearing test, the worker must avoid significant noise exposure for the stated period so the audiogram reflects stable hearing rather than a temporary shift caused by recent noise.

accident-related bilateral hearing-loss.description_plain_english: For hearing loss caused by an accident or injury, rate each affected ear separately and add the percentages if both ears are affected.
accident-related bilateral hearing-loss.how_the_guide_uses_it: When an accident injures both ears, the guide allows the losses from the two ears to be brought into the same hearing assessment instead of treating only one ear in isolation.

already-evaluated-elsewhere rule.description_plain_english: The CNS chapter says an impairment rating should not include impairments that have already been evaluated in other areas.
already-evaluated-elsewhere rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor not to give a second award for a problem that has already been captured under another neurological category or another chapter.

anal disease class rule.description_plain_english: Anal disease ratings focus on whether there is gas or stool leakage, whether symptoms are controlled by treatment, and how complete the faecal incontinence is.
anal disease class rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor to place the condition into the correct severity class for anal disease. The class chosen controls the percentage range, so symptoms, objective findings, treatment intensity, and functional impact must match the class description.

asbestosis or silicosis minimum 10% rule.description_plain_english: A worker with radiologically definite asbestosis or silicosis can receive at least 10% incapacity even if symptoms are absent and pulmonary function looks normal.
asbestosis or silicosis minimum 10% rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule sets a floor of 10% once the guide’s stated criteria for this dust-related lung disease are met, so qualifying cases are not rated below that level.

asbestosis or silicosis profusion thresh.description_plain_english: For an award in asbestosis or silicosis, the x-ray profusion should be at least 1/1 on the ILO classification.
asbestosis or silicosis profusion thresh.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule requires the chest-imaging profusion score to reach the guide’s threshold before the disease is treated as compensable under that table.

better-ear rule for noise induced deafne.description_plain_english: For noise-induced deafness, assess only the better ear using the dedicated NID column of the table.
better-ear rule for noise induced deafne.how_the_guide_uses_it: For noise-induced deafness, the guide uses the better ear in the way specified by the hearing chapter so compensation reflects overall binaural hearing rather than the worse ear alone.

biliary tract disease class rule.description_plain_english: Biliary disease ratings depend on whether episodes are occasional, recurrent, irreparable, or causing progressive liver damage and persistent jaundice.
biliary tract disease class rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor to place the condition into the correct severity class for biliary tract disease. The class chosen controls the percentage range, so symptoms, objective findings, treatment intensity, and functional impact must match the class description.

both-eyes visual cap rule.description_plain_english: When the percentages for both eyes are added together, the total should not exceed 100%.
both-eyes visual cap rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This cap prevents the final visual award for both eyes together from exceeding the chapter’s maximum allowed value, even if several visual deficits are present.

bronchodilator-only occupational asthma.description_plain_english: Occupational asthma controlled only with bronchodilators may be rated at 5%.
bronchodilator-only occupational asthma.how_the_guide_uses_it: If occupational asthma is controlled with bronchodilator use alone, the guide places the case in the corresponding low-severity award bracket instead of a higher medication-based class.

cap at amputation value.description_plain_english: The total rating for injuries to a body part must not exceed the rating for losing that whole body part.
cap at amputation value.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule prevents the calculated impairment for an injured part from exceeding the value the guide assigns to losing that part completely.

colonic and rectal disorder class rule.description_plain_english: Colon and rectum ratings depend on how often symptoms occur, how badly bowel function is disturbed, whether pain is present, how much activity is limited, and whether there are constitutional effects such as fever, anaemia, or weight loss.
colonic and rectal disorder class rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor to place the condition into the correct severity class for colonic and rectal disorders. The class chosen controls the percentage range, so symptoms, objective findings, treatment intensity, and functional impact must match the class description.

diplopia correction rule.description_plain_english: Diplopia is rated differently depending on whether it is expected to be correctable by prisms or surgery and where in the field of gaze it occurs.
diplopia correction rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: If double vision is corrected by prisms or another accepted method, the guide tells the assessor to rate the person using the corrected situation rather than the uncorrected complaint alone.

headache validity rule after neurologica.description_plain_english: For persistent post-concussion or headache complaints, the examiner must check whether the symptoms fit known anatomy and physiology, stay consistent over time, and are not contradicted by observed behaviour or examination findings.
headache validity rule after neurologica.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule makes the assessor look for consistency, neurological context, and supporting evidence before treating headache as a compensable long-term deficit after brain injury.

hearing compensation threshold rule.description_plain_english: Compensation is payable only when the average hearing loss at 1, 2, and 3 kHz reaches 50 dB or more.
hearing compensation threshold rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This threshold rule means hearing loss must reach the guide’s minimum compensable level before any award is made.

hearing stabilisation rule.description_plain_english: Hearing should be assessed only when the loss has stabilised and is not expected to improve further.
hearing stabilisation rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: The guide requires hearing to be medically stable before final assessment, so the result is based on lasting loss rather than early fluctuation.

herniation class rule.description_plain_english: Hernia ratings depend on whether the protrusion is occasional or persistent, whether it is reducible, and whether it limits daily activities.
herniation class rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor to place the condition into the correct severity class for herniation. The class chosen controls the percentage range, so symptoms, objective findings, treatment intensity, and functional impact must match the class description.

high-dose inhaled steroid or combination.description_plain_english: Occupational asthma requiring high-dose inhaled steroids or inhaled combination therapy may be rated at 15%.
high-dose inhaled steroid or combination.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule places occupational asthma into a higher award band when the condition needs high-dose inhaled steroids or combination controller therapy to stay controlled.

higher-award rule.description_plain_english: When two alternative ways of rating the same problem are possible, use the one that gives the higher justified award, not both together.
higher-award rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: When more than one allowed method can rate the same problem, the guide tells the assessor to choose the higher valid award rather than add both together.

liver disease class rule.description_plain_english: Liver disease ratings depend on objective evidence of chronic or progressive liver disease, recent major complications such as jaundice, ascites, or variceal bleeding, nutritional strength, blood tests, and nervous-system effects of liver failure.
liver disease class rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor to place the condition into the correct severity class for liver disease. The class chosen controls the percentage range, so symptoms, objective findings, treatment intensity, and functional impact must match the class description.

low-dose inhaled steroid occupational as.description_plain_english: Occupational asthma requiring low-dose inhaled steroids may be rated at 10%.
low-dose inhaled steroid occupational as.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule assigns occupational asthma to the guide’s corresponding medication-based class when control requires low-dose inhaled steroid treatment.

most-severe-cerebral-category rule.description_plain_english: For brain-related impairment, the guide first looks across four cerebral-function areas and takes the most severe one as the cerebral impairment rating.
most-severe-cerebral-category rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: In the cerebral-function tables, the assessor uses the category that best matches the person’s most severe accepted deficit, rather than stacking overlapping cerebral categories on top of one another.

MRI requirement for back injuries.description_plain_english: For back injuries, an MRI scan is required so the assessor can judge the seriousness of the injury and rate any lasting disability more accurately.
MRI requirement for back injuries.how_the_guide_uses_it: For the specified back-injury situations, the guide requires MRI evidence before certain spinal findings can be used in the rating.
aliases: magnetic resonance imaging rule for back injuries

no-duplication rule.description_plain_english: Do not count the same functional problem twice under two different headings.
no-duplication rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This is an anti-double-counting rule. The assessor must not award separate percentages for different labels that describe the same underlying loss of function.

objective-over-subjective rule.description_plain_english: When symptoms and tests do not line up perfectly, the guide says to give more weight to objective findings than to symptoms alone.
objective-over-subjective rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: Where symptoms and objective evidence do not match, the guide tells the assessor to rely more heavily on measurable findings such as scans, laboratory results, spirometry, or examination signs.

occupational asthma maintenance-medicati.description_plain_english: If occupational asthma still needs daily long-term medication even after the worker has been away from the causative exposure for a year or more and further improvement is unlikely, the guide allows a mild impairment award even when FEV1 is above 80% predicted.
occupational asthma maintenance-medicati.how_the_guide_uses_it: For occupational asthma, the long-term maintenance medicine needed to keep the condition under control helps determine the award level.

oral steroid occupational asthma award.description_plain_english: Occupational asthma requiring oral steroids may be rated at 20%.
oral steroid occupational asthma award.how_the_guide_uses_it: If occupational asthma requires oral steroids, the guide treats this as a more severe level and assigns the corresponding higher award range.

pain rule.description_plain_english: Pain is not usually given a separate extra award if the relevant injury category already includes pain. Pain can sometimes be reflected through loss of movement, but not twice.
pain rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: Pain on its own is not rated as a separate free-standing award unless the guide specifically allows it. Instead, pain is usually reflected only through the functional problem it causes.

pain-clinic referral rule for intractabl.description_plain_english: Hard-to-treat post-concussion headache cases should be referred to a pain clinic for assessment and treatment before deciding that maximal medical improvement has been reached.
pain-clinic referral rule for intractabl.how_the_guide_uses_it: For severe persistent headache cases, the guide expects specialist pain-management input before concluding that the headache is truly intractable.

per-eye visual cap rule.description_plain_english: The guide says the percentage incapacity for one eye should not exceed 50%.
per-eye visual cap rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This cap prevents the award for a single eye from exceeding the maximum value the visual chapter allows for one eye.

permanent total incapacity additional co.description_plain_english: If the worker is certified as having permanent total incapacity of 100%, the law gives an extra 25% compensation amount on top of the normal amount payable.
permanent total incapacity additional co.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule identifies situations where the worker may qualify for extra compensation because the accepted condition results in permanent total incapacity rather than partial incapacity.

presbycusis correction rule.description_plain_english: For workers aged 50 or more with noise-induced deafness, subtract 0.5% for each year above age 50 to correct for age-related hearing loss.
presbycusis correction rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule adjusts hearing assessment to account for age-related hearing decline, so compensation reflects the injury- or work-related component rather than ordinary ageing alone.

renal causation-sharing rule.description_plain_english: If kidney damage could have more than one cause, the guide says each potentially injurious factor should be assumed to contribute part of the damage.
renal causation-sharing rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: If the kidney problem is only partly caused by the work injury or occupational disease, the guide allows only the work-related share to be compensated.

renal higher-class rule.description_plain_english: If creatinine clearance, serum creatinine, and chronic kidney disease stage point to different impairment classes, the higher class is used.
renal higher-class rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor to place the condition into the correct severity class for renal higher-class rule. The class chosen controls the percentage range, so symptoms, objective findings, treatment intensity, and functional impact must match the class description.

renal provisional-award rule.description_plain_english: The renal chapter says the first assessment should be a provisional award, followed by reassessment about six months later. A final award is given only after the condition has stabilised.
renal provisional-award rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule allows a temporary or provisional kidney-related award when the condition has not yet fully stabilised but the guide permits interim assessment.

respiratory class rule.description_plain_english: To place a worker into a respiratory class, the worker does not have to meet every criterion in that class. At least one key pulmonary-function measure must be abnormal enough to fit that class.
respiratory class rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor to place the condition into the correct severity class for respiratory. The class chosen controls the percentage range, so symptoms, objective findings, treatment intensity, and functional impact must match the class description.

solitary-kidney 10% rule.description_plain_english: A person with a solitary kidney is rated as having 10% permanent incapacity, and that value can be combined with other relevant permanent-incapacity values.
solitary-kidney 10% rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: Loss of one kidney, or the accepted equivalent situation in the chapter, attracts a baseline 10% award under the rule stated there.

spine bladder-bowel add-on rule.description_plain_english: For certain spine injury categories, add 10% to 25% when there is neurogenic bladder or bowel incontinence, depending on whether it is incomplete or complete and whether bladder alone, bowel alone, or both are involved.
spine bladder-bowel add-on rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: If a spinal injury also causes accepted bladder or bowel dysfunction, the guide allows that additional deficit to be added in the way the spinal chapter specifies.

spine higher-category rule.description_plain_english: If a spinal injury seems to fit more than one spine category, use the category that gives the higher justified award.
spine higher-category rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: If a spinal case could fit more than one category, the assessor chooses the higher supported category instead of averaging the categories.

spine monoparesis division-by-2 rule.description_plain_english: In certain spinal cord categories, if the cord-related weakness is only monoparesis, the listed disability award is divided by 2.
spine monoparesis division-by-2 rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: Where the chapter instructs, impairment from weakness affecting one limb only is halved to reflect monoparesis rather than more extensive paralysis.

spine non-contiguous segment combination.description_plain_english: If separate non-adjacent spinal segments were injured in the same accident and both materially contribute to disability, the guide says to combine them using the Combined Values Chart.
spine non-contiguous segment combination.how_the_guide_uses_it: If separate non-adjacent parts of the spine are independently injured, the guide allows their accepted values to be combined using the prescribed method.

tinnitus not compensable rule.description_plain_english: The guide says associated tinnitus is not compensable on its own.
tinnitus not compensable rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule says tinnitus by itself does not attract a separate hearing award under this guide.

upper digestive tract class rule.description_plain_english: Upper-digestive ratings depend on symptoms, the need for diet or drugs, weight loss, and whether treatment controls the condition.
upper digestive tract class rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: This rule tells the assessor to place the condition into the correct severity class for upper digestive tract disorders. The class chosen controls the percentage range, so symptoms, objective findings, treatment intensity, and functional impact must match the class description.

visual timing rule.description_plain_english: Visual-function assessment should usually take place 6 to 8 weeks after the injury or emergency surgery; definitive corrective surgery does not need to have happened yet.
visual timing rule.how_the_guide_uses_it: The visual chapter requires assessment at the proper time after injury or treatment so vision has stabilised and the result reflects lasting loss.

ankylosis sequence.description_plain_english: The step-by-step method for rating a joint that is fixed in one position.
ankylosis sequence.how_the_guide_uses_it: For a frozen joint, the guide tells the assessor to first identify the joint position, then read the matching table value, and then compare that result with any alternative method if the chapter allows one. This keeps the ankylosis assessment in a fixed order.
step_sequence: Measure how far the fixed joint deviates from neutral in each relevant direction using a goniometer.
Look up the percentage for each measured fixed position in the ankylosis table.
Take only the largest percentage as the rating for that joint.
Do not add ankylosis percentages across directions for the same joint.

central nervous system 5-step sequence.description_plain_english: The guide’s step-by-step order for rating cerebral impairment.
central nervous system 5-step sequence.how_the_guide_uses_it: For central nervous system injuries, the guide uses a five-step workflow: identify the main neurological problem, choose the matching category, rate each relevant function, avoid counting the same deficit twice, and then combine the accepted values using the guide’s method.
step_sequence: Check for problems with consciousness, awareness, episodic loss of consciousness, or sleep/arousal.
Assess mental status and highest integrative function.
Assess language problems such as aphasia or dysphasia.
Assess emotional or behavioural problems that change brain function.
Choose the most severe cerebral category and then combine it with distinct neurological impairments in Group 5 using the Combined Values Chart.

Combined Values Chart sequence.description_plain_english: The method for combining two or more ratings using the chart.
Combined Values Chart sequence.how_the_guide_uses_it: When more than two percentages have to be combined, the guide tells the assessor to combine the first two values, then combine that result with the next value, and continue step by step until one final percentage remains.
step_sequence: Identify the larger impairment value and find it on the side of the chart.
Find the smaller value along the bottom of the chart.
Read across and down to the intersection to get the combined value.
If there are three or more values, first combine the two highest values.
Then combine that result with the next value.
Repeat until all values have been combined.

digital sensory loss sequence.description_plain_english: The method used to rate sensory loss in the fingers.
digital sensory loss sequence.how_the_guide_uses_it: For loss of feeling in a finger or toe, the guide tells the assessor to identify the affected area, assign the local sensory-loss value, and then convert that local value into the appropriate whole-person or limb-related percentage.
step_sequence: Test the palmar side of the finger using two-point discrimination.
Identify which digital nerve or nerves are affected.
Classify the sensory loss as total, partial, or none based on the test distance.
Use the guide’s finger maps and values.
For partial sensory loss, give 50% of the value for total sensory loss.

peripheral nerve assessment sequence.description_plain_english: The method used to rate a nerve or plexus injury.
peripheral nerve assessment sequence.how_the_guide_uses_it: For a peripheral nerve injury, the assessor works in order: identify the injured nerve, assess motor loss and sensory loss separately where required, apply the relevant table limits, and then combine accepted components without double counting.
step_sequence: Identify the affected nerve or nerve plexus.
Assess sensory loss and motor loss.
Decide whether each loss is partial or total.
Use the guide’s maximum values for that nerve.
Give a proportion of the maximum; for partial loss that interferes with activity, 50% of the listed value can be used.

restriction of motion sequence.description_plain_english: The step-by-step method for rating reduced joint movement.
restriction of motion sequence.how_the_guide_uses_it: For joint stiffness, the guide tells the assessor to measure movement with the proper method, compare the loss with the chapter table, total the permitted movement losses, and then cap the result where the guide requires it.
step_sequence: Put the joint in the neutral position for the movement being tested.
Measure movement from neutral with a goniometer.
If the joint cannot reach neutral, record the nearest fixed angle and then measure the arc of motion from there.
Look up the matching incapacity percentage in the joint-specific table.
Repeat for each movement direction.
Add the percentages for the different directions to get the total for restriction of motion of that joint.

ckd-stage.description_plain_english: Chronic Kidney Disease staging from 1 (mildest — structural damage with normal GFR ≥ 90 mL/min) to 5 (kidney failure, GFR < 15 mL/min).
ckd-stage.how_the_guide_uses_it: Under GATIOD Chapter 7, CKD stage is used together with biological investigations and clinical signs to determine the governing severity class for renal permanent impairment. When CKD stage, serum creatinine, and creatinine clearance point to different impairment classes, the higher class governs.
